current.text: Experts call him a category league bust at a rank in the 20s. They see him as reasonable in the 40s and would not take him in the first two rounds.
He went for 27 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
Josh would only pay about 21 to 22 USD for him in an auction.
An expert does not expect him to get huge minutes this season.
OKC's frontcourt is crowded. Hartenstein, Holmgren and Jaylin Williams form the center rotation, with Al Horford re-signed and Thomas Sorber also on the roster.
Hartenstein's role looks secure next to him.
An expert feels good about him keeping his block rate this season.
He had a poor playoff series against San Antonio. His coach says nobody on the team is more trusted to improve over the summer.
Ryland expects the playoff series to motivate him. He is not yet in his prime and should keep improving.

durable.text: Experts rate him the second-best rim protector in the NBA, with great positioning. Josh calls him an All-NBA player.
He can shoot a bit from outside and is a decent scorer.
Blocks are his league outlier category, far above the top 250 pool.
His blocks make him look better in plain 9-cat z-score rankings than his real head-to-head worth.
He made 55% of his twos in the season he broke his hip. In the next season he went back to 65%.
The 55% on twos from the broken hip season is probably an outlier.

note: Our league paid 32 USD for him last season, and Yahoo values him at 29 USD (rank 31). The experts see a rank in the 40s and about 21 to 22 USD as fair, closer to ESPN's rank 52, so let someone else pay 30 USD. He fits any build as an elite shot blocker who helps rebounds and FG% without hurting other categories. Before the draft on 2026-10-18, check his quadriceps status (Yahoo Q). Early in the season, watch his minutes in a crowded OKC frontcourt.
